title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Severe sepsis and pneumonia.

Vitals:
Temperature: 101.4 F
Blood Pressure: 110/70 mmHg
Heart Rate: 92 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 20 breaths/min
SpO2: 95% on room air

Recent Labs:
WBC: 14,500
Creatinine: 2.4 mg/dL (on admission), 1.1 mg/dL (on discharge)
BUN: 38 mg/dL
Lactate: 2.8 mmol/L
Hemoglobin: 11.8 g/dL

Review of Systems:
The patient reports productive cough, shortness of breath, and generalized fatigue. She denies chest pain, palpitations, or lower extremity edema. She denies any urinary symptoms or neurological deficits.

Social History:
The patient lives at home with her spouse. She is a former smoker (quit 10 years ago) and denies current alcohol or illicit drug use.

Family History:
Mother had hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Father had a history of coronary artery disease.

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 77-year-old female admitted with severe sepsis secondary to a community-acquired pneumonia. Upon admission, she presented with significant tachypnea and fever. Laboratory evaluations and clinical presentation indicated the development of acute kidney injury (AKI) triggered by the systemic infection. Sputum and blood cultures were obtained; however, no specific organism grew during the course of the stay. The patient was managed with broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics and aggressive fluid resuscitation. Her renal function showed steady improvement over the week, and her kidney function recovered to near-baseline levels by the time of discharge. She remained hemodynamically stable throughout the hospitalization and was able to tolerate oral intake.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Severe sepsis
2. Pneumonia
3. Acute kidney injury (AKI)

Discharge Medications:
1. Amoxicillin 500mg PO three times daily
2. Lasix 40mg PO daily
3. Atorvastatin 20mg PO daily

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a repeat renal function panel and a chest X-ray to monitor the resolution of the pneumonia.

Electronically signed, E. Castillo, MD, 05/18/2026
explanations: Severe sepsis: the sepsis code A41.9, plus R65.20 because an acute organ dysfunction (kidney injury) is caused by the sepsis; no shock.

distractors.why: The sepsis caused an acute organ dysfunction: add R65.20.
